raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The `multimodal-gen-test-2-npu-a3` PR test job currently runs on `linux-aarch64-a3-800t-16` (16-NPU) runners, but every test case in suite `2-npu` uses at most 2 NPUs:

- All 6 parametrized cases in `test_server_2_npu.py` use `num_gpus=2` (tp_size=2, ulysses_degree=2, or ring_degree=2, with all HCCL communication done within a single node).
- The standalone case `test_glm_image_distributed.py` occupies exactly 2 NPUs (AR on gpu 0 via `--base-gpu-id 0`, denoiser on gpu 1 via `--num-gpus 1 --base-gpu-id 1`), and its skip guard only requires `device_count() >= 2`.

Keeping this job on 16-NPU runners wastes scarce `a3-800t-16` resources that are contended by heavy suites such as acc-8 / acc-16. The repo already runs `multimodal-gen-test-1-npu-a3` and `base-c-test-acc-2-npu-a3` on `linux-aarch64-a3-800t-2` runners, so the 2-NPU runner pool is available and proven.

## Modifications

- `.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml`: change `runs-on` of the `multimodal-gen-test-2-npu-a3` job from `linux-aarch64-a3-800t-16` to `linux-aarch64-a3-800t-2`.
- Keep the matrix partitions (`part: [0, 1]`) and all other job settings unchanged. The per-shard estimated runtime (~20 min) is well below the 60-minute step timeout, so no timeout adjustments are needed.

Note: `minimax_h3_t2va_2npu` and `mova_360p_ti2va_2npu` rely on host memory for layerwise offloading; if the 2-NPU nodes have less host RAM, those two cases are the ones to watch in the CI result.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A (CI workflow configuration change only; no model or kernel code affected). The `multimodal-gen-test-2-npu-a3` job itself serves as the regression test.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. Test cases run with identical NPU model and count as before; wall-clock time per shard is unchanged since partitions run on separate machines either way.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
